Whenever a character is able to select an archetype feat, they can select aetherfont archetype feats. Like regular archetypes, the feat selection provided can give the characters mechanical and thematic focuses in developing their characters.  In general, aetherfont archetype feats tend to emphasize use of focus points and their aetherfont features in specific ways. 

Selecting an aetherfont archetype is significant enough that it behaves similarly to a class archetype in that it is a decision made at 1st level, even though it may not alter the class the way a class archetype would. As a result, it restricts the character from selecting any other aetherfont or class archetypes. When characters select an aetherfont archetype, they must take the dedication for that archetype at 1st or 2nd level.

Amongst those who walk with nature, there are some who ponder their greater place in the cosmos of all life. The Sojourner is a believer of nature and its core elements, seeking union with the great harmony. They pursue the wisdom of the bending river of all life with great zeal, and fight valiantly to protect it as if they were part of its core. They travel and fight alongside chosen stalwart companions, journeying together to be part of the circle of life.

The Arcblade is a dedicated blademaster who harnesses the power of storms, wielding metallic bladed weaponry as a conduit for fearsome control of electricity and water. The art was said to have originated amongst an order of swordsmen known as the Blades of Krymmenos, who were blessed by an azure drachiri protector. Over the course of history, this knowledge has been passed on to smaller circles of fighters, keeping it secluded from the prying eyes of the world. The art of the Arcblade is half spectacle as it is deadly. With lightning-fast strikes, electrifying sorcery and dazzling channeling of tides, an opponent will never see the Arcblade’s true intention until the fight is over in a flash of light.

In numerous Ardorean cultures, unity with spirits is a defining tenet. Many mythologies and cultural tenets revolve around the harmony between man and spirit, and how both ensure their mutual survival and their destruction. In these cultures, there are those whose entire purpose is to alleviate difficulties or enforce boundaries, by becoming emissaries that travel with representatives of spiritual domains domains through a powerful pact. Whether it’s a summoned spirit, a cherished animal companion, or a special familiar, a Convoker is one that channels the powers of the domains through their partner to see their ideals realized. The companion may be in servitude to greater forces, or perhaps the agent of such actions themselves, but they are unable to perform this task on their own; thus, the Convoker becomes their conduit for their sacred task.

Dragons of Ardor are beings of magic; never ceasing in their affiliation with ether that radiates from their very bodies. In that, the Drachiri Empire took to great advantage in moulding the world to their whims, even creating other draconic creatures or suffusing their champions with their magic. Among these are those who take a dragon’s influence to their very limits, where one bonds so closely to a dragon that they can channel powers beyond their wildest dreams. A Drachensoul need not be a Draichsar nor a Draich, but they must be one who has an immutable bond with a dragon that still lives or persists spiritually, whether through a pact or dangerous therianization. The result is a mutable power that grows with each draconic influence.

When the Empty exiles arrived on the shores of Garrunga, they found themselves in a dangerous land. Their allies were the gangoran tribes who saw their Emptiness as a hidden gift, and one tribe shared with the new settlers their ways of gunpowder. For decades, the Gangoran tribes had used gunpowder to hunt for great beasts in the earliest forms of firearms and explosives, to create great alchemical powders for use by their dreaming warriors, or to mine the depths of Garrunga’s caverns. With gunpowder, oil, metal and steam, the sygican settlers began to thrive. Since then, gunpowder and ranged weaponry became part and parcel of their armaments, even wielded by their non-empty descendants. Those speaking Domish had coined the term ‘Fusilier’ for those who bore these weapons in their day to day. When sygican technology flourished, this discipline evolved further, spreading across the world. To many, Fusiliers resemble the unification of the talents and hardship that the sygican had undergone in their quest to cement their place in Ardor’s history, not forgotten.

The fabric of the world is written in runes, or so it is said. When runes were discovered, their potential was exploited to the fullest, and it only grew as runic magic was used to create magic one could only dream of. For in their use, anything could be commanded upon the tapestry so long as one knew how to. But such things lead to untold destruction and the unraveling of the boundaries between realms. As Oblivion yawned upon a battlefield, and as an entire nation was levelled, the world collectively came together to restrict the use of runic magic. Knowledge of the art was greatly restrained and kept secret over centuries, and laws were passed to forbid unsanctioned uses. And yet, there are those who still practice in secret or under the auspices of nations willing to bend law or to enact it to the extent that it is still legally justifiable. Such are the Runescribes; bearers of the forbidden language, who can delve into the magic that defines reality.
